paragraphs: I'm an IT professional with more than 20 years of experience across systems analysis, database management, application development, IT project management and digital strategy, in banking, financial services and pharmaceuticals in Singapore and the Philippines.

Today I'm a Digital Channel Lead at Boehringer Ingelheim, looking after the governance and optimisation of owned digital channels (web, email and mobile messaging) across the ASKAN region: ASEAN, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

Along the way I've enjoyed writing training materials, running onboarding and knowledge-transfer sessions, and mentoring colleagues. So I've started teaching: since October 2026 I've been a part-time mentor at Mapúa Malayan Digital College, handling Object-Oriented Systems Analysis and Design. I'm also taking a Master of Information Systems at UP Open University to grow into a full IT faculty role.

approach.title: Model the system before building it

facts: My first IT job, in 2006, was as a programmer at the Philippines' Commission on Audit.
I'm a big Neil Gaiman fan. If you want a book that's dark, funny and strange all at once, ask me for a recommendation.
I've watched over end-of-day batch jobs in 22 countries, from New Zealand to the Netherlands.
Spanish and Italian are my favourite cuisines, and I don't just eat them — I cook them too.
I went from Front-End Developer to Digital Channel Lead at Boehringer Ingelheim in about four years.
I'm a sucker for horror movies. The creepier the house, the happier I am.
I've written code in COBOL and in JavaScript, two languages born more than 35 years apart.
I sing a lot, mostly when no one's around. My kitchen and my shower are always sold-out venues.
This will be my fourth degree. Yes, I like school.
I also love a good period film: grand houses, gorgeous costumes and people saying a lot with a single look.
I've been on 24/7 support rotations, so I know what a 3 a.m. alert feels like.
My kitchen is my favourite test environment. Paella and pasta are both in my production release.
I've worked with at least seven database systems, from Oracle and Sybase to Greenplum.
My ideal movie night is a double feature: a horror film, then a period drama to calm my nerves.
I've been connected to Boehringer Ingelheim for over ten years: five as a consultant, then as an employee.
If you hear someone singing while stirring a risotto, there's a good chance it's me.
I got my BS and MS in IT from the same university, two years apart.
I'm a student and a teacher at the same time: learning at UPOU while mentoring at Mapúa Malayan Digital College.
I've lived and worked in two countries: the Philippines and Singapore.
I've done UAT for so many releases that I read test scripts for fun. Almost.
